title: The Market Believes In the Dodgers. Not So Much the Brewers, Rays, White Sox and Cubs.
contentHtml:
Everybody loves a late-season pennant chase, and so we’ve all spent the last month or so of MLB’s regular season focused on the final remaining playoff races — particularly the division battles in the AL Central and AL West, with some wild-card and seeding intrigue thrown in on the side for good measure.

Subscribe now

But as we now rapidly approach the playoffs proper, which begin next Tuesday, the truth is that a lot of those races will soon be rendered beside the point. Instead, the central question will be more around which playoff-bound teams are capable of making a deep run come October. And depending where you look, you can arrive at some very different answers.

Focus on the 2026 regular season, and the Milwaukee Brewers have generally been the best team in baseball, a tick better than the two-time defending champion L.A. Dodgers. They went into Wednesday leading MLB in winning percentage, schedule-adjusted run differential and Elo rating — and while the Dodgers had more Wins Above Replacement (WAR), at the very least one might think L.A. and Milwaukee were co-favorites.

Indeed, that’s what the Elo ratings think after moving every team’s strength estimates around all season long, based on the results, run differentials and locations of each game. (Starting at a regressed prior from the end of last season.) According to Elo on Wednesday, Milwaukee (19.6 percent) was just a slightly better pick to win the World Series than Los Angeles (19.2), with the Tampa Bay Rays a bit behind at 13.3 percent. But at the same exact time, that’s not really how the betting and prediction markets see it.
